_note_cytassist: The two `cytassist-*-outs/` directories were added by #257 as the committed evidence for the per-slide-design rendered spot diameters (70 um for the 6.5 mm CytAssist V4 slide, 60 um for the 11 mm V5). Neither ships a vendor IMAGE: the scale check that is their reason for existing reads only the positions table and the scalefactors, and the one CytAssist-specific image is one this importer will never emit (see the `cytassist_image.tiff` entries).

measured.nearest_neighbour_estimator: registration_qc.measure_spot_pitch, THE SHIPPED ONE, over the complete committed table. Recorded because an earlier revision of this record carried a figure from a throwaway helper that RANDOM-SUBSAMPLES above 6,000 points — it read 363.2988 here where the shipped estimator reads 363.0771, and the test band was loose enough (rel=0.01) to let the wrong number sit in the file. A blind audit caught it. Both figures in this block are now recomputed by the test at rel=1e-9 against the estimator that actually runs.
measured.note: `implied = spot_diameter_fullres * 100 um / measured_pitch_px` — the same arithmetic #222 used to fix 65.0, against the slide's manufactured 100 um pitch, which 10x's Space Ranger glossary states for 'Visium v1 and v2 capture areas' alike. TWO estimators are recorded because they are not the same measurement: `same_row` is the centre-to-centre pitch BY CONSTRUCTION (the distance to the `array_col +- 2` neighbour in the same `array_row`), while `nearest_neighbour` — the estimator `registration_qc` uses — is the DIAGONAL neighbour, which on this lattice sits up to ~0.5% low of the pitch because the rendered hex lattice is not exactly equilateral. The same-row figure is the one to compare against the design's constant; the nearest-neighbour figure is the one the shipped scale check will report.

cytassist-v4-outs/spatial/scalefactors_j.why_it_is_here: Issue #257. This bundle is the committed evidence for the 70 um rendered spot diameter of slide design `visium-6.5mm-70um-rendered-spot`. Its `fiducial_diameter_fullres / spot_diameter_fullres` is 3/2 (exact in IEEE-754 double), which is what identifies the design; `regist_target_img_scalef` is present, which is what identifies the assay as CytAssist. See docs/design/visium-slide-design-scale.md.

cytassist-v4-outs/spatial/tissue_positio.subset_note: COMPLETE, and that is the point. It was a 170-row contiguous window until a blind audit showed that a producer switching its numerator on `len(positions) >= 1000` — a threshold no windowed fixture reaches — passed the whole test suite AND the cross-package gate while applying a 21.4% wrong micron scale to every real vendor bundle. That is #243's lesson exactly (an undersized image fixture hid an incoherent artifact for months), one file over. The full table is 10x's own documented row count for this capture area, so the fixture is now a real bundle in the dimension that hid the defect. The `.h5` stays a subset: the filtered matrix legitimately holds fewer barcodes than the positions table, which is the shape the standard fixture has too.
cytassist-v4-outs/spatial/tissue_positio.what: The vendor's COMPLETE 4992-row tissue_positions.csv, byte-identical. Not a subset.

coherence.why_it_is_here: Issue #243 — before this file, no committed artifact in the repo had a real tissue image and its real spots geometrically coherent.

spatial/tissue_hires_image.png.history: Until #243 this path held a 200x200 PNG, measured to be a bit-identical PIL Resampling.BICUBIC 10x downscale of this file. The downscale left tissue_positions.csv and scalefactors_json.json untouched, so the bundle's own spots mapped to a 1000 px frame the 200x200 image could not cover and ZERO of its 160 spots landed on it. tests/test_image_coherence.py asserts the coherence and asserts that the same predicate still rejects that 10x downscale.

spatial/tissue_lowres_image.png.why_not_committed: The vendor emits it and it is equally coherent, but committing it would break `tests/test_absence_is_absence.py`'s assertion that this bundle emits EXACTLY ONE image (it ships a hires image and no lowres). That assertion is worth more than a second real image, and #243 is closed by the hires image alone. `test_image_coherence.py`'s FIXTURE_BUDGET_BYTES is set below (current fixture size + the `bytes` below) so that adding it fails a test rather than happening quietly.
